ai_summary.headline: Cash is almost absent from Chad's plan: MPCA is 0.2% of requirements and shows no funding in FTS.
ai_summary.narrative: The 2026 HNRP asks for USD 986M and is about 45% funded, but most of that sits in the refugee response [s2][s3]. MPCA is the only separately costed cash line at USD 1.82M, 0.18% of the plan, after a 2025 MPCA component of USD 5.7M received nothing; the target fell from 104,800 to 33,444 people [s1]. FTS shows no funding to the MPC cluster [s3]. Yet H1 2025 reporting cited 46 partners delivering about USD 11.4M in cash to 228,230 people, which suggests the plan understates real cash activity [s1]. The sharpest recent signal is the USD 100M US-OCHA allocation, of which USD 18.8M is cash and USD 4.5M MPCA, now being assessed by CALP with the CWG [s5][s6]. The CWG is government-led with a leadership handover to MASSAH under way, and reports declining funding as its main challenge [s4]. There appears to be little recent evidence on modality preference, cost efficiency or markets.
barriers: MPCA unfunded in 2025 and no funding visible in FTS for 2026 [s3]
No aggregated CVA figure in the HNRP, so cash is hard to track [s1]
CWG leadership transition to government not complete [s4]
No modality preference or cost-efficiency data found
opportunities: The CALP and CWG assessment of the USD 100M allocation can inform the next pooled allocation [s5]
Large sectoral cash footprint (food security USD 18 per person per month) could anchor a consolidated CVA figure [s1]
data_gaps: Plan document not independently opened (figures via gDCF analysis)

total_funding_usd.note: All incoming funding to the plan, pledges excluded. Matches the FTS plan summary.

mpc_usd.note: No multi-purpose cash cluster with funding is visible on FTS for this plan (the plan may still carry an MPC requirement), so MPC funding cannot be seen.

ctp_usd.note: All flows tagged 'Cash transfer programming (CTP)', inside or outside the MPC cluster.

sectoral_cva_usd.note: Flows whose FTS modality field is 'Cash transfer programming (CTP)' and whose destination cluster is not multi-purpose cash: 30 flows. The CTP tag is set by the reporting donor or agency and is not applied consistently, so this is a floor, not a measure of sectoral cash. Largest: Sécurité Alimentaire US$3.2M, Abris AME US$0.9M, Protection US$0.8M.

cva_usd.note: Union of the MPC cluster and the CTP tag. Widest defensible FTS cash figure; still a floor because untagged sectoral cash is invisible.

cva_pct_of_total.note: cva_usd as a share of total plan funding.

sectoral_cva_pct_of_total.note: sectoral_cva_usd as a share of total plan funding.

mpc_pct_of_total.note: MPC cluster funding as a share of total plan funding (single-cluster view).

fts_cva.caveat: FTS records funding, not transfers to people, and only to first-level recipients. Sectoral cash depends on a modality tag that reporters apply unevenly.

fsps.name: Moov Money (Moov Africa Chad)
used_by: Government of Chad / PARCA project (World Bank-funded)
fsps.evidence: Paid 120,000 FCFA to 22,000 vulnerable N'Djamena households (Aug 2021) and 45,000 FCFA per refugee / 120,000 FCFA per host household at Guilmey (Jun 2022). Government social-protection / refugee-support transfers, not a named humanitarian agency. Both sources are government/World Bank social-protection or refugee programmes (PARCA), not NGO or UN humanitarian cash.

cva_to_local_pct.note: Indicator 4.2 proxy. Share of FTS cash funding (MPC cluster or CTP tag, US$5.3M) whose first-level recipient is a local or national NGO/CSO or a national government body. FTS does not see sub-grants, so this understates money that reaches local actors through international intermediaries.
